title: Score-Based Density Estimation from Pairwise Comparisons
claim: Latent preferences observed only through pairwise comparisons yield a tempered winner density, which a position-dependent tempering field links to the target belief.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, multiplication and equals signs between panels forming an equation
description: Four square panels in a row, joined by a multiplication sign and an equals sign so they read as an equation. Panel (a), 'Problem setup', has a dark purple background with cyan-to-magenta contour lines of a banana-shaped belief density on the left. The handwritten text 'my belief' has a dashed arrow pointing at the contours. Two white X marks labeled A and B sit below, with a 'succeeds' symbol and the quote 'more probable' between them. Panel (b), 'MWD', is a dense scatter of blue samples with small cyan score arrows on a dark background, with faint green-yellow clusters on the left and right. Panel (c), 'Tempering field', is a smooth plasma-colored heatmap with two bright yellow-orange crescents and a dark center. Panel (d), "'Tempered' MWD", shows blue samples concentrated on two crescent-shaped modes. The eye goes first to the bright heatmap and the 'my belief' text.
caption: (a) Problem setup. An expert holds a subjective belief over a parameter space, such as the likely hyperparameters of a learning algorithm (e.g. learning rate and weight decay), and can answer questions like "Do you expect configuration A or B to work better?". We learn their belief as a density, to be used e.g. as a prior distribution for finding optimal hyperparameters. (b)-(d) Density estimation from $200$ uniformly sampled pairwise comparisons, with the target density shown as a heatmap. (b) Samples and the score field at an intermediate noise level $\sigma$, for a diffusion model trained on the (winner, loser) pairs to model the marginal winner density (MWD). (c) Estimated tempering field. (d) Samples from the score-scaled annealed Langevin dynamics with the MWD score and a tempering field estimate. Samples align well with the target density, demonstrating the fundamental relationship between the scores of the estimable MWD and the latent target (belief density).
abstract: We study density estimation from pairwise comparisons, motivated by expert knowledge elicitation and learning from human feedback. We relate the unobserved target density to a tempered winner density (marginal density of preferred choices), learning the winner's score via score-matching. This allows estimating the target by `de-tempering' the estimated winner density's score. We prove that the score vectors of the belief and the winner density are collinear, linked by a position-dependent tempering field. We give analytical formulas for this field and propose an estimator for it under the Bradley-Terry model. Using a diffusion model trained on tempered samples generated via score-scaled annealed Langevin dynamics, we can learn complex multivariate belief densities of simulated experts, from only hundreds to thousands of pairwise comparisons.
